tour.abraham.0: About 1950 BC, Ur of the Chaldeans near the mouth of the Euphrates: in the early morning a small family caravan leaves the city gate, seen from behind and at a distance. An old man, a younger man and woman and a youth walk beside laden donkeys and a few sheep, in long fringed wool robes and head cloths. Behind them rises the great stepped mudbrick ziggurat of Ur above flat-roofed houses, with date palms, irrigation canals and reed boats on the river. No camels, no horses, no domes or minarets. Painted in the manner of nineteenth-century biblical watercolour illustration, warm natural light, soft earth tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.abraham.1: About 1925 BC, Haran on the Balikh River in upper Mesopotamia: a walled trading town of mudbrick on a low mound, with flat roofs and a busy gate where donkey caravans unload bales of wool and copper. Outside the walls, the family's black goat-hair tents stand among grazing sheep in a wide, dry plain. In the foreground, at a respectful distance, a small group in wool mantles mourns beside a shrouded body laid on a reed mat, heads bowed. No camels saddled like modern ones, no domes or minarets, no Roman arches. Painted in the manner of nineteenth-century biblical watercolour illustration, warm natural light, soft earth tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.abraham.2: About 1920 BC, Shechem in the central hill country of Canaan: in a green valley between two mountains stands a great old oak, the oak of Moreh. Beneath it a white-bearded man in a wool mantle and head cloth, seen from behind, kneels beside a newly built altar of rough uncut fieldstones, a thin column of smoke rising. A soft shaft of golden light falls through the branches, showing the divine presence; his household of herdsmen, women and flocks of sheep and goats stands back in awe. God not shown as a figure, no carved or dressed stones, no temple buildings. Painted in the manner of nineteenth-century biblical watercolour illustration, warm natural light, soft earth tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.abraham.3: About 1920 BC, the hill country between Bethel and Ai in Canaan: a wide view of terraced limestone ridges dotted with olive and terebinth trees. On a saddle between two hills, black goat-hair tents are pitched, with sheep, goats and donkeys grazing. To the west on one hill a small walled town, to the east another; between them a man in a wool mantle stands at a simple altar of heaped fieldstones, small figures of his household nearby. Evening light, a thin smoke rising. No dressed masonry altars, no medieval castles, no domes. Painted in the manner of nineteenth-century biblical watercolour illustration, warm natural light, soft earth tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.abraham.4: About 1920 BC, the Nile delta in Middle Kingdom Egypt: a wide view of a painted Egyptian palace court with lotus-bud columns, whitewashed walls and palm trees beyond. Egyptian officials in white linen kilts and shaved heads escort a Semitic woman in a long coloured wool dress and head cloth toward the palace, while her husband, a bearded herdsman in a fringed mantle, watches from a distance among his donkeys. Darkened clouds gather above the palace hinting at coming plagues. No pyramids being built, no camels, no Greek or Roman columns, no legible hieroglyphs. Painted in the manner of nineteenth-century biblical watercolour illustration, warm natural light, soft earth tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.abraham.5: About 1919 BC, a ridge near Bethel in Canaan: two bearded men in wool mantles stand on a hilltop seen from behind, one pointing east down to the green, well-watered Jordan plain shimmering far below toward the Dead Sea basin. Their herdsmen and large flocks of sheep and goats, donkeys and tents fill the slopes, already dividing into two companies. On the right, a distant path leads south toward the oak groves of Mamre near Hebron. No camels, no walled medieval cities, no modern roads. Painted in the manner of nineteenth-century biblical watercolour illustration, warm natural light, soft earth tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.abraham.6: About 1872 BC, a rocky mountain top in the land of Moriah, the later site of Jerusalem: a white-bearded old man in a wool mantle stands beside a rough fieldstone altar stacked with wood, a boy sitting unharmed nearby, both seen from a distance and partly from behind. The old man turns toward a thicket where a ram is caught by its horns. A brilliant light breaks through the clouds above, implying the voice from heaven. Bare limestone hills, scrub and a donkey left below. No knife raised toward the boy, no buildings or temple on the hill, no winged angel. Painted in the manner of nineteenth-century biblical watercolour illustration, warm natural light, soft earth tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.abraham.7: About 1820 BC, Hebron in the hill country of Canaan: a funeral procession, seen from a distance, carries a shrouded body on a wooden bier toward the dark mouth of a rock-cut cave in a terraced field with olive trees. Two grown men in wool mantles walk at the head, one with the bearing of a desert herdsman, the other with a shepherd's crook; mourners in head cloths follow with bowed heads. Late afternoon light, sheep on the slopes. No Herodian enclosure wall or mosque over the cave, no domes, no Roman tombs. Painted in the manner of nineteenth-century biblical watercolour illustration, warm natural light, soft earth tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.jacob.0: About 1760 BC, Beersheba in the dry Negev of southern Canaan: at the edge of a tent encampment beside a stone-lined well, a young man in a wool tunic and mantle with a staff and a small bundle walks away north into the open land, seen from behind. Outside a black goat-hair tent an old, blind father sits, and a mother stands watching with her hand raised. Far off on a ridge, a burly hunter figure with a bow looks on darkly. Tamarisk trees, flocks, low hills. No camels saddled like modern ones, no horses, no stone houses. Painted in the manner of nineteenth-century biblical watercolour illustration, warm natural light, soft earth tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.jacob.1: About 1760 BC, Luz in the stony hill country of Canaan: night on a bare hillside strewn with limestone boulders. A young traveller in a wool mantle lies asleep on the ground, his head on a stone, seen small in the lower part of the scene. From the ground beside him a wide stairway of radiant light rises into a starry, glowing sky, with luminous wingless figures going up and coming down upon it. The top dissolves into brilliant light, divine presence without any figure. No wings, no halos, no city, no Gothic or medieval imagery. Painted in the manner of nineteenth-century biblical watercolour illustration, warm natural light, soft earth tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.jacob.2: About 1760 BC, a well in the open fields near Haran in upper Mesopotamia: a large round stone has just been rolled from the mouth of a well, and a young man in a travel-worn wool mantle waters a flock of sheep while a young shepherdess in a long wool dress and head cloth stands beside her flock, seen at mid-distance. Other shepherds lean on their staffs with flocks waiting. Wide plain, distant mudbrick walls of a town, afternoon light. No camels saddled like modern ones, no buckets on pulleys, no medieval dress. Painted in the manner of nineteenth-century biblical watercolour illustration, warm natural light, soft earth tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.jacob.3: About 1740 BC, the wooded hills of Gilead east of the Jordan: two groups of herdsmen, women and children face each other on a hillside among oaks, with large flocks of sheep and goats and loaded donkeys behind. Between them two bearded men in wool mantles stand beside a heap of gathered stones and an upright standing stone, raising their hands in oath, seen from a distance. Women in head cloths sit on donkeys. Evening light over the ranges. No horses, no swords drawn, no carved inscriptions or legible writing on the stones. Painted in the manner of nineteenth-century biblical watercolour illustration, warm natural light, soft earth tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.jacob.4: About 1740 BC, the ford of the Jabbok in the rugged hills of Gilead: first light of dawn over a rocky stream bed and a deep ravine with oleanders. On the far bank, two figures grapple and wrestle in silhouette, one a man in a wool tunic, the other a mysterious figure faintly luminous, seen from a distance. The sky is breaking pale gold behind them. On the opposite side, the family's tents and flocks wait in shadow. No wings, no halo, no armour or weapons, no modern bridge. Painted in the manner of nineteenth-century biblical watercolour illustration, warm natural light, soft earth tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.jacob.5: About 1740 BC, open country near the Jabbok east of the Jordan: a burly bearded man in a rough mantle has run out ahead of four hundred men and embraces his brother around the neck, both weeping, seen at mid-distance. The brother's wives and children stand behind on the slope with flocks and donkeys, watching. Further down the valley, simple booths of branches and reed shelters for cattle are being built at Succoth. Warm late light. No horses or cavalry, no stirrups, no medieval armour. Painted in the manner of nineteenth-century biblical watercolour illustration, warm natural light, soft earth tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.jacob.6: About 1739 BC, Shechem in the central hills of Canaan: a broad valley between two mountains, the walled Middle Bronze Age town of Shechem with thick earthen ramparts and a stone gate in the distance. In a field before the town, a bearded man in a wool mantle and his sons build a simple altar of uncut fieldstones, while a townsman counts out pieces of silver into his hand beside them. Tents, flocks and women in head cloths nearby. No coins, no dressed stone temple, no domes. Painted in the manner of nineteenth-century biblical watercolour illustration, warm natural light, soft earth tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.jacob.7: About 1732 BC, beneath an oak near Shechem, then the hills of Bethel in Canaan: Jacob's household, men and women in wool tunics and head cloths, kneel and bury small clay and metal figurines and earrings in a pit beneath a great oak, seen from a distance. On the hill above, an old man stands by a pillar of stone with oil poured over it, and a soft radiance falls from the sky upon him. God shown only as light. No large carved idols, no temple, no legible writing. Painted in the manner of nineteenth-century biblical watercolour illustration, warm natural light, soft earth tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.jacob.8: About 1732 BC, the road to Ephrath, which is Bethlehem, in the Judean hills: a family caravan halted beside a stony road among terraced hills and olive trees. In the distance, women in head cloths gather around a tent; a newborn is held up wrapped in cloth. Nearby, a grieving bearded man sets an upright standing stone over a fresh grave of heaped stones, seen from behind. Grey evening sky, donkeys waiting. No church, no domed tomb building, no inscriptions. Painted in the manner of nineteenth-century biblical watercolour illustration, warm natural light, soft earth tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.jacob.9: About 1716 BC, Mamre near Hebron in the hill country of Canaan: under great oaks, two bearded brothers in middle age, one in a rough hunter's mantle and one in a herdsman's wool cloak, walk side by side at the head of a burial procession carrying a shrouded body toward a rock-cut cave, seen from a distance. Mourners with flocks and tents behind, olive terraces, golden late light. No mosque, no Herodian walls, no domes or minarets. Painted in the manner of nineteenth-century biblical watercolour illustration, warm natural light, soft earth tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.joseph.0: About 1727 BC, the vale of Hebron in the hill country of Canaan: outside a cluster of goat-hair tents among olive trees, an old man in a wool mantle sends off a youth wearing a long tunic woven in bands of many colours, red, blue and ochre, seen from behind as he sets out along a path north. Older brothers' empty grazing grounds behind, a few servants and sheep. Morning light over terraced hills. No Renaissance dress, no horses, no modern patchwork patterns. Painted in the manner of nineteenth-century biblical watercolour illustration, warm natural light, soft earth tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.joseph.1: About 1727 BC, the pastures near Dothan in northern Samaria: a group of bearded shepherds in wool tunics draw a youth up from a dry cistern in the ground, while a caravan of Ishmeelite traders with camels loaded with bundles of spices, balm and myrrh halts on the road beside them, seen from a distance. One brother holds out his hand for silver. Wide green valley, hills beyond. No violence shown, no camels saddled like modern ones, no coins, no medieval dress. Painted in the manner of nineteenth-century biblical watercolour illustration, warm natural light, soft earth tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.joseph.2: About 1727 BC, a Middle Kingdom Egyptian town by the Nile: in the courtyard of a wealthy official's house, with whitewashed walls, papyrus-bundle columns, a garden pool and palm trees, a young Semitic servant in a plain linen kilt oversees granaries and scribes counting sacks, seen from a distance. Egyptian servants in white linen, a household official watching approvingly from a shaded portico. No pyramids under construction, no Greek or Roman architecture, no legible hieroglyphs or writing. Painted in the manner of nineteenth-century biblical watercolour illustration, warm natural light, soft earth tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.joseph.3: About 1714 BC, the royal court of Middle Kingdom Egypt: a vast hall with painted lotus columns, a Pharaoh on a raised throne wearing the nemes headcloth, courtiers and magicians in white linen standing back. In the centre, small in the scene, a young clean-shaven Semitic man in white linen raises his hand as he speaks. Beyond the open colonnade, the Nile with fields of ripe grain. No Greek or Roman columns, no legible hieroglyphs or writing, no anachronistic gold crowns. Painted in the manner of nineteenth-century biblical watercolour illustration, warm natural light, soft earth tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.joseph.4: About 1705 BC, a granary hall in Egypt: ten bearded Canaanite men in coloured wool tunics and mantles, with empty sacks and donkeys, bow to the ground before an Egyptian governor seated on a raised dais, clean-shaven in white linen and a broad collar, seen from the side and at a distance. Behind him, scribes and rows of sealed mudbrick grain silos. Warm dusty light. No pyramids being built, no legible writing, no Roman architecture. Painted in the manner of nineteenth-century biblical watercolour illustration, warm natural light, soft earth tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.joseph.5: About 1704 BC, a reception room of a governor's house in Egypt: Egyptian servants in white linen are leaving through a doorway. In a hall with painted columns, a clean-shaven man in fine white linen stands weeping with arms open toward eleven bearded Canaanite brothers in wool mantles who stand back in astonishment and fear, one young brother being embraced, seen at mid-distance. Sacks of grain on the floor. No legible writing, no Roman architecture, no crowns. Painted in the manner of nineteenth-century biblical watercolour illustration, warm natural light, soft earth tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.joseph.6: About 1704 BC, Beersheba in the Negev of southern Canaan: night over a large encampment by a well and tamarisk trees, ox-drawn Egyptian carts, donkeys, tents and flocks. An old man in a wool mantle kneels beside a fieldstone altar where a fire burns, seen from behind, as a soft column of light descends from the starry sky, God shown only as light. Family members sleep around tents. No camels saddled like modern ones, no spoked chariot wheels on the carts, no buildings. Painted in the manner of nineteenth-century biblical watercolour illustration, warm natural light, soft earth tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.joseph.7: About 1704 BC, the land of Goshen in the eastern Nile delta: a wide fertile landscape of green pastures, canals and papyrus marshes, date palms and mudbrick villages. A large Hebrew family with flocks of sheep and goats, cattle and loaded donkeys settles in, pitching tents, while Egyptian officials in white linen point out the land. An old patriarch is seen from behind leaning on a staff. No pyramids nearby, no Roman features, no camels saddled like modern ones. Painted in the manner of nineteenth-century biblical watercolour illustration, warm natural light, soft earth tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.joseph.8: About 1688 BC, Hebron in the hill country of Canaan: a great funeral procession winds up through terraced hills toward a rock-cut cave in a field with olive trees. Egyptian elders and dignitaries in white linen with broad collars mingle with Hebrew men in wool mantles; a shrouded bier is carried at the front by sons, seen from a distance. Mourners raise their hands in lament. No Herodian enclosure, no mosque or domes, no stirrups or riders on horseback. Painted in the manner of nineteenth-century biblical watercolour illustration, warm natural light, soft earth tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.exodus.0: About 1490 BC, Rameses in the eastern Nile Delta, at dawn after the first Passover: a vast column of Hebrew families streams out past the mudbrick walls and granaries of the store city they built as slaves. People in plain wool and linen tunics and mantles, head cloths, kneading troughs bound in cloth on their shoulders, flocks of sheep and goats, donkeys laden with bundles. Lintels of low mudbrick houses still marked with dark stains of blood. Egyptian pylon gateway and palm groves in the distance, Delta canals catching the low sun. Figures small, seen from behind as they walk east. No camels, no horses ridden by the Hebrews, no chariots among them. Painted in the manner of nineteenth-century biblical watercolour illustration, warm natural light, soft earth tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.exodus.1: About 1490 BC, Etham on the edge of the wilderness east of the Nile Delta, at dusk: the Israelite camp of low black goat-hair tents spreads across sandy scrubland, cooking fires, sheep and goats penned with thorn brush. Above the camp a tall column of soft glowing fire rises into the darkening sky, lighting the people who stand small and still looking up at it; behind them the last daylight fades over flat Delta land, ahead the empty desert. Wool mantles, women with water jars, donkeys tethered. Divine presence only as the pillar of fire, no figure within it. No modern tents, no camels with modern saddles. Painted in the manner of nineteenth-century biblical watercolour illustration, warm natural light, soft earth tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.exodus.2: About 1490 BC, the sea near Pi-hahiroth at the edge of Egypt, in grey morning light: a wide path of dry seabed runs between two towering walls of green water, and long lines of Israelite families with flocks and donkeys climb out onto the far shore, small figures seen from behind and above. Behind them the waters are crashing back together, white foam swallowing the distant shapes of Egyptian two-wheeled chariots and horses. A great dark cloud stands over the scene, lit from within. Late Bronze Age Egyptian chariots with six-spoked wheels, Hebrews in wool tunics and mantles. No drowned bodies shown, no gore, no stirrups, no medieval armour. Painted in the manner of nineteenth-century biblical watercolour illustration, warm natural light, soft earth tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.exodus.3: About 1490 BC, the wilderness of Shur in western Sinai: in the foreground at the pool of Marah, Moses, an old man in a wool mantle, casts a small leafy tree into a still pool while thirsty people with empty clay jars and waterskins watch from the rocky bank. Beyond, across the pale desert, the scene opens toward the oasis of Elim: a grove of date palms around clear springs where tents are already being pitched and flocks drink. Wide landscape, figures small. Dry acacia scrub, limestone hills, harsh light softening toward the green oasis. No modern wells, no stone fountains, no camels with modern saddles. Painted in the manner of nineteenth-century biblical watercolour illustration, warm natural light, soft earth tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.exodus.4: About 1490 BC, Rephidim in the granite valleys of southern Sinai: on a rocky hilltop Moses sits on a stone with both arms raised, Aaron and Hur on either side holding up his tired arms, all three seen small from behind against the evening sky. Below in the wide wadi a battle sways back and forth between Israelites and Amalekite raiders with spears, slings and shields, kept distant and dusty, no blood. Nearby a stream runs from a split red granite rock where families fill jars. Wool tunics, leather belts, bronze spearheads. No horses, no iron armour, no stirrups. Painted in the manner of nineteenth-century biblical watercolour illustration, warm natural light, soft earth tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.exodus.5: About 1490 BC, the plain before Mount Sinai: a great jagged granite mountain rises, its summit wrapped in thick dark cloud shot through with fire and lightning, smoke rising as from a furnace. On the plain the vast Israelite camp of goat-hair tents, the people standing far back at a boundary, small figures bowed or gazing up in awe. In the middle distance at the mountain's foot, the tabernacle courtyard of white linen hangings on posts and the tent of goat-hair and skins, an altar smoking before it. Divine presence only as cloud, fire and light, no figure. No buildings of stone, no temple columns, no Gothic forms. Painted in the manner of nineteenth-century biblical watercolour illustration, warm natural light, soft earth tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.exodus.6: About 1489 BC, Kadesh-barnea, an oasis on the edge of the Negev: twelve dusty men return to the tent camp, two of them carrying between them on a pole a huge cluster of grapes, with pomegranates and figs in baskets. A crowd gathers, some faces turned away in dismay, people with arms raised in protest, while two men stand apart urging them on. Beyond, the barren hills of the wilderness stretch toward Canaan. Wool tunics and mantles, goat-hair tents, springs and a few palms. Figures mid-size, seen from a distance. No horses, no stone city in the camp. Painted in the manner of nineteenth-century biblical watercolour illustration, warm natural light, soft earth tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.exodus.7: About 1451 BC, Mount Nebo in the highlands of Moab: an aged Moses in a wool mantle and staff stands alone on a bare limestone summit, seen from behind and small, looking west over a vast hazy panorama: the Jordan valley far below, the green oasis of Jericho, the Dead Sea glinting to the south, and the hills of Canaan fading into blue distance. Golden late light, wind in sparse scrub. Below on the plain the far-off Israelite camp. Divine presence only as warm light breaking through clouds. No monuments, no churches, no modern roads. Painted in the manner of nineteenth-century biblical watercolour illustration, warm natural light, soft earth tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.exodus.8: About 1450 BC, the Jordan opposite Jericho in spring flood season: priests in white linen carry the gold-covered ark on poles and stand still in the middle of the riverbed, which lies dry; upstream the water stands heaped up far away. Long lines of Israelites with flocks and donkeys cross the bare riverbed toward the green palm oasis of Jericho on the west bank, its walled tell on the horizon. Some men carry large stones from the riverbed. Figures small in a wide valley. Ark plain and partly draped, no figures shown on it in detail. No bridges, no boats, no Roman buildings. Painted in the manner of nineteenth-century biblical watercolour illustration, warm natural light, soft earth tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.conquest.0: About 1450 BC, Jericho at night: the steep mudbrick city wall with houses built into it, a small window high in a house on the wall. A woman in a dark wool robe and head covering leans from the window letting down a thick rope, and two men in plain mantles slip down the outside of the wall toward the dark palm groves below. A scarlet cord is visible at the window. On the flat roof behind her, bundles of flax stalks laid out to dry. Moonlight, distant torches of searchers at the gate. Figures small, seen from below at a distance. No medieval stone castle walls, no glass windows. Painted in the manner of nineteenth-century biblical watercolour illustration, warm natural light, soft earth tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.conquest.1: About 1450 BC, Gilgal in the Jordan valley near Jericho, in spring: the Israelite camp of goat-hair tents beside a circle of twelve large river stones. Families gather at evening around fires to keep the Passover, roasting lambs, eating unleavened bread. In the foreground people harvest and parch ripe barley ears from the fields of the plain and bake flat loaves on hot stones; empty baskets lie where the manna used to be gathered. Date palms, the hills of Moab behind in pink evening light. Wool and linen garments. Figures mid-size, seen from a distance. No churches, no stone buildings. Painted in the manner of nineteenth-century biblical watercolour illustration, warm natural light, soft earth tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.conquest.2: About 1450 BC, Jericho on the seventh day: a long procession of Israelites circles the walled city on its mound, priests in white linen blowing curved ram's horn trumpets, the ark carried on poles among them, the people with arms raised in a great shout. Part of the mudbrick wall is collapsing outward in clouds of dust. On one stretch of wall that still stands, a house with a scarlet cord at its window. Date palms of the oasis around. Figures small, seen from a distance across the plain. No metal trumpets, no stone castle towers, no gore. Painted in the manner of nineteenth-century biblical watercolour illustration, warm natural light, soft earth tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.conquest.3: About 1450 BC, Ai in the central hill country east of Bethel, morning: the small walled town on a rocky ridge with its gate open as its defenders rush out downhill after a retreating Israelite force. Behind the town, from a hidden ravine among olive trees and boulders, a second band of Israelites streams toward the empty gate, and the first smoke rises from inside the walls. On a nearby hill a figure holds up a spear as a signal. Wool tunics, bronze spears and javelins, slings. Figures small in a wide hill landscape. No horses, no iron armour, no blood. Painted in the manner of nineteenth-century biblical watercolour illustration, warm natural light, soft earth tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.conquest.4: About 1450 BC, Mount Ebal above Shechem in the central hills: on the slope Joshua stands beside a large altar of uncut fieldstones, reading aloud from a scroll (no legible writing), smoke rising from offerings. Below in the narrow valley, the priests with the ark stand between two great crowds of Israelites ranged on the slopes of Ebal and the facing Mount Gerizim, women and children among them, all small figures listening. Terraced hills, olive trees, the walls of Shechem in the valley. Wool mantles and head cloths. No hewn-stone temple, no columns, no legible writing. Painted in the manner of nineteenth-century biblical watercolour illustration, warm natural light, soft earth tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.conquest.5: About 1449 BC, the hills around Gibeon, morning after an all-night march: Joshua's army sweeps up the slopes toward the hilltop town while the Amorite forces flee down the descent of Beth-horon, scattering under a sky full of falling hailstones. The sun hangs strangely still and bright over Gibeon, the pale moon over the Aijalon valley to the west. Small figures with bronze spears and shields, wool tunics, dust everywhere, seen from a distance. Terraced limestone hills and olive groves. Divine presence only in the light and hail. No horses ridden, no medieval armour, no blood. Painted in the manner of nineteenth-century biblical watercolour illustration, warm natural light, soft earth tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.conquest.6: About 1445 BC, Hazor in upper Galilee: the great Canaanite city on its high mound burns, smoke and flames rising from its palace and mudbrick walls. In the foreground by the marshy waters of Merom, the remains of a broken Canaanite camp: overturned two-wheeled chariots, horses running loose, and Israelite foot soldiers in wool tunics with bronze spears moving away toward the city. Mount Hermon faint and snowy in the north. Figures small, seen from a distance. No stirrups, no iron plate armour, no blood or bodies. Painted in the manner of nineteenth-century biblical watercolour illustration, warm natural light, soft earth tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.conquest.7: About 1444 BC, Shiloh in the hill country of Ephraim: on a level terrace the tabernacle stands within its courtyard of white linen hangings, the tent of goat-hair and skins behind a smoking bronze altar. Before it, Joshua and the high priest Eleazar stand by while lots are drawn from a vessel, and representatives of the tribes gather around in groups. Men also set off carrying survey notes on tablets (no legible writing). Terraced hills, olive and vine slopes. Wool mantles, head cloths. Figures small to mid-size, seen from a distance. No stone temple, no domes. Painted in the manner of nineteenth-century biblical watercolour illustration, warm natural light, soft earth tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.ruth.0: About 1160 BC, Bethlehem in the Judean hills during a famine: parched terraces and withered barley fields around the small hill village of stone and mudbrick houses. On the dusty road leading east toward the hills of Moab, a small family walks away, seen from behind: a man in a wool mantle leading a laden donkey, a woman with a head covering, two young sons. Dry olive trees, empty threshing floor. Distant across the haze, the Dead Sea and the Moab plateau. Figures small. Iron Age four-room houses with flat roofs. No domes, no churches, no camels. Painted in the manner of nineteenth-century biblical watercolour illustration, warm natural light, soft earth tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.ruth.1: About 1150 BC, a road in the highlands of Moab leading west toward the Jordan: three widows in dark wool mantles and head coverings stand at a fork in the road. One young woman walks away back toward a distant village, glancing back; the other young woman clings to the older woman, holding her arm, refusing to leave. Wide rolling plateau, wheat stubble, a lone terebinth tree, the Dead Sea far below in haze. Figures small, seen from a distance, no faces filling the frame. Simple bundles, a water skin. No camels, no medieval dress. Painted in the manner of nineteenth-century biblical watercolour illustration, warm natural light, soft earth tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.ruth.2: About 1150 BC, barley fields outside Bethlehem in spring: reapers in short wool tunics cut barley with sickles and bind sheaves, young women follow behind. A young Moabite woman in a simple head covering stoops to glean stalks left at the field's edge, a bundle under her arm. Figures small to mid-size, seen from a distance. Iron Age flint-and-iron sickles. No scythes, no windmills.
